candidates.failure_scenario: Line 58 says 'Add a key ... and fund that address at the faucet ... Then write a realm:', and the block under it opens on `gnokey add alice`. A visitor who added and funded alice pastes the block: gnokey asks 'Override the existing key "alice" [Y/n]:', whose empty answer is yes (tm2/pkg/commands/utils.go GetConfirmation), so Enter replaces the funded key with a new unfunded address; addpkg then signs as an unfunded alice whose address is not the <your-g1-addr> namespace the visitor substituted, and the deploy fails. The keybase is shared across chains, so any existing 'alice' is replaced. A visitor who named the key otherwise gets a second, unfunded alice that addpkg signs with. whatsnew_test.sh:222 stubs gnokey as `exit 0`, so its 'the deploy block runs' check passes. The merge-base page has no `gnokey add`.
